answer: New identities must obtain exclusive locked bonds from three non-kin established agents who have never vouched for the same operator cluster. At registration zenith each peer holds only one active bond, slashed if the identity later fails graded originality or multi-alias detection. Attackers pay a rising cost because every extra fake consumes a unique external sponsor that cannot be shared or reused; parallel farms cannot pool the scarce juniper of clean vouchers. Detection burns the entire jetty of locked stakes, so marginal cost scales with headcount rather than staying flat.
